The degree is offered through Georgetown’s School of Foreign Service, ranked first in the world for international relations master’s programs by Foreign Policy in 2024

Press Release

DOHA, Georgetown University in Qatar (GU-Q), a Qatar Foundation partner university, will launch the Master of Arts in International Politics and Security in fall 2027. The degree is offered through Georgetown’s School of Foreign Service, ranked first in the world for international relations master’s programs by Foreign Policy in 2024.

Dr. Hend Zainal, Executive Director, Strategy, Management and Partnerships within Qatar Foundation’s Higher Education division, said: “Georgetown University in Qatar has shown academic leadership in recognizing when developments in Qatar and the wider region call for a new academic program. The decision to bring international politics and security together in one graduate degree draws on that regional knowledge and gives the program timeliness and relevance – making it a benchmark in the wider study of international affairs for other higher education institutions.”

“Georgetown University’s foreign service degrees are respected around the world. The ambition for this master’s is to earn a place alongside them. This is a hallmark of Education City’s impact: a university’s experience in Qatar can shape what it offers the world.”

“In partnership with Qatar Foundation, we are excited to launch our first research-oriented graduate degree culminating in an original thesis,” said Interim Dean Clyde Wilcox. “The program will draw on Georgetown’s strengths in international relations and the expertise of our faculty across a range of disciplines, advancing our shared commitment to education and research in service of Qatar and the wider region.”

Students complete 36 credits over two years of full-time study or three years of part-time study, culminating in individual thesis supervision and a policy report assessed against professional standards.

“We designed this program around a simple idea: We live in a world where rigorous scholarship and real-world policy expertise are more necessary than ever,” said Valentini Pappa, Program Director for New Academic Initiatives. “Our MA meets those needs. With a focus on faculty mentorship, small seminars, policy simulations and practitioner engagement, we will ensure that we prepare graduates to understand and shape the political and security challenges facing Qatar, the region and the world.”

The program is open to all qualified applicants, including recent graduates entering directly from their undergraduate studies. Applicants may come from a wide range of academic backgrounds, including international relations, political science, history, law, economics, area studies, sociology, data science and technology, as well as public service.

GU-Q expects a cohort drawn from the Gulf and beyond, including professionals from ministries, diplomatic services, civil society and the private sector. The program will prepare graduates for roles in government and diplomacy, multilateral organizations, think tanks and research centers, and the private sector, as well as for doctoral study.

“Our new MA in International Politics and Security is perfectly timed and designed to meet the needs of young scholars and practitioners in Qatar and beyond,” said Rory Miller, Professor of International Politics. “They are passionate about finding solutions to the challenges of living in a contested and increasingly multipolar world, marked by high levels of insecurity, rapid changes in technology, the nature of warfare and energy markets, and the growth of nontraditional threats.” 

Applications open Jan. 15, 2027. The priority deadline is April 15, and the final deadline is June 15. More information, including admissions requirements, is available on the program website.

About Georgetown University in Qatar Established in 2005, Georgetown University in Qatar (GU-Q) is the leading global campus for the university, offering a Bachelor of Science in Foreign Service (BSFS) with majors in International Politics (IPOL), International Economics (IECO), Culture and Politics (CULP), International History (IHIS), and Science, Technology, and International Affairs (STIA).   GU-Q also provides an Executive Master’s program in Diplomacy and International Affairs, and a number of customized professional development programs for public and private sector entities.

About Qatar Foundation – Unlocking Human Potential

Qatar Foundation for Education, Science and Community Development (QF) is a nonprofit organization focused on education, research and innovation, and community development that supports Qatar on its journey to becoming a diversified and sustainable economy. Across its ecosystem, which comprises more than 50 entities, QF strives to serve the people of Qatar and beyond through its work in progressive education, sustainability, artificial intelligence, precision health care and social progress.

QF was founded in 1995 by His Highness Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, the late Father Amir of Qatar, and Her Highness Sheikha Moza bint Nasser, who shared a vision to provide Qatar with quality education. This vision has evolved into a globally unique, multidisciplinary ecosystem of knowledge offering opportunities for lifelong learning, fostering innovation and empowering people to be socially engaged citizens and drivers of positive change.

This diverse and interconnected ecosystem comprises a world-class education landscape spanning the full spectrum of learning, from preschool to postdoctoral level; research, innovation and policy centers addressing global challenges; and community facilities for people of all ages to seek knowledge, embrace active lifestyles and expand their horizons within QF’s Education City, which spans 12 square kilometers in Doha, Qatar. Through a unique approach to multidisciplinary, global education, Education City represents Qatar Foundation’s large-scale legacy investment focused on building human capacity for the future of Qatar, the region and the world.
